summaries_kept.root: This is the root of an appliance/system manual whose chapters — Installation and Setup, System Requirements, Network Configuration, Storage and Backup, Security and Access Control, Monitoring and Alerting, Scaling and Load Balancing, Data Import and Export, API Reference, Troubleshooting, Upgrade Procedures, and Compliance and Audit — all restate the same six-part operating model over differing entity vocabularies: (1) each component carries a bounded queue and, once it fills, requests are rejected with the documented back-pressure status; (2) each component is reconciled against a named registry on fixed intervals of 5, 15, 30, or 60 seconds; (3) each component writes its state to a named successor before acknowledging the write to the caller; (4) on failover a named successor takes over outstanding requests within one heartbeat interval; (5) tuning balances a counterpart's throughput against the memory the component reserves for in-flight work; and (6) operators size each component so that named peers do not saturate it during peak traffic. Installation and Setup applies this model to chassis, front panel, kickplate, cable harness, mounting rail, and power supply across Unpacking the Unit, Rack Preparation, First Power-On, Initial Configuration, and Firmware Update; System Requirements applies it to kernel, node, volume, scheduler, memory pool, and interface entities across Supported Hardware, Operating Systems, Memory and Storage, Network Interfaces, Environmental Limits, and a Safety Notice; Network Configuration covers addressing, Routing, Firewalls and Ports, TLS Termination, and service discovery over resolver, certificate, listener, gateway, subnet, and endpoint variants; Storage and Backup covers manifest, volume, bucket, snapshot, journal, and tier artifacts in warm/cold/immutable/compressed variants; Security and Access Control covers token, principal, policy, credential, role binding, and audit trail artifacts plus a Copyright and Trademarks notice; Monitoring and Alerting covers window, probe, sink, counter, gauge, and dashboard components in per-tenant, sampled, streamed, and cumulative variants plus a Glossary of Terms; Scaling and Load Balancing covers shard, queue, pool, replica, scheduler, and limiter in elastic, pinned, saturated, and under-provisioned variants; Data Import and Export covers Supported Formats, Chunked Ingestion, Schema Mapping, Export Pipelines, Validation Runs, and a Safety Notice; API Reference covers Authentication, Core Endpoints, Pagination, Error Semantics, and Rate Limits over request, response, header, cursor, envelope, and status code entities; Troubleshooting covers Diagnostic Commands, Common Failures, Log Analysis, Escalation Path, Known Issues, and Revision History over ticket, diagnostic, probe, trace, stack trace, and runbook entities; Upgrade Procedures covers Version Matrix, Rolling Upgrades, Rollback Plan, Compatibility Notes, and Post-Upgrade Checks over canary, health check, manifest, migration, release, and replica set components in rolling, reversible, deprecated, and staged variants; and Compliance and Audit covers Retention Policy, Data Residency, Evidence Collection, Control Mapping, Certification Status, and a Glossary of Terms over scope, ledger, control, residency region, evidence bundle, and attestation components. Concrete facts stated across these chapters include: snapshots are retained 35 days by default; the platform needs at least 16 GiB of memory per node; a session stays valid for 30 minutes without a refresh; a paginated page carries at most 200 items; Routing requires ports 7946 (cluster protocol), 2380 (peer channel), and 9090 (metrics) open between nodes; the Safety Notice (repeated in System Requirements and Data Import and Export) requires disconnecting the power supply and verifying the grounding conductor before maintenance, states the unit contains no user-serviceable components, and warns that opening the chassis voids the warranty and exposes the operator to electric shock; the Copyright and Trademarks notice (repeated verbatim ten times) reserves all rights, prohibits reproduction or transmission in whole or part without prior written permission, and states product names and logos belong to their respective owners; and the Revision History (repeated in Storage and Backup and Troubleshooting) lists Version 1.0 initial release, 1.1 clarified the configuration examples, 1.2 added the troubleshooting chapter, 2.0 restructured the deployment sections, and 2.1 editorial corrections throughout.
summaries_kept.sec-00112: This section collects the System Requirements / Operating Systems requirements, overview, and procedure content covering volumes, nodes, interfaces, kernels, schedulers, and memory pools. Write acknowledgement is always ordered: the node writes to the supported node, the scheduler to the supported scheduler, the volume to the physical scheduler, the scheduler to the recommended memory pool, the kernel to the supported node, the node to the supported interface, the interface to the minimal interface, the node to the minimal memory pool, and the memory pool to the supported node — each before acknowledging the write to the caller. Failover always completes within one heartbeat interval: interface failover is taken over by the physical scheduler, the minimal kernel, the physical kernel, or the supported memory pool; scheduler failover by the physical node; kernel failover by the physical memory pool; node failover by the supported interface; volume failover by the minimal interface. Bounded queues exist on minimal nodes, recommended kernels, minimal schedulers, supported memory pools, and physical kernels, each rejecting requests with the documented back-pressure status once full. The platform requires at least 16 GiB of memory per node. Sizing guidance: size the memory pool so a recommended scheduler or minimal volume does not saturate it at peak traffic, the scheduler so a minimal kernel does not saturate it, the interface so a recommended interface does not saturate it, and the volume so a recommended node does not saturate it. Tuning the volume balances physical, recommended scheduler, or minimal interface throughput against the memory the volume reserves for in-flight work; tuning the interface balances supported volume throughput against memory the interface reserves; tuning the kernel balances physical scheduler throughput against memory the kernel reserves. Reconciliation intervals: the minimal interface every 5 seconds against the volume registry, the minimal memory pool every 5 seconds against the interface registry, the physical volume every 15 seconds against the volume registry, and the recommended volume and minimal memory pool every 30 seconds against the memory pool registry.
summaries_kept.sec-00193: The Network Configuration / Routing section states that ports 7946 for the cluster protocol, 2380 for the peer channel, and 9090 for metrics must be open between nodes, and defines back-pressure, tuning, write acknowledgment paths, failover takeovers, reconciliation intervals, and sizing. Bounded queues that reject with the documented back-pressure status once full apply to the static certificate, static resolver, public listener, and private subnet. Write paths (state written before acknowledging to the caller): resolver→public certificate, certificate→static endpoint, certificate→private subnet, listener→private certificate, endpoint→public endpoint, endpoint→private gateway, subnet→static resolver, certificate→static gateway, resolver→private subnet, subnet→dynamic gateway, resolver→static subnet, and resolver→static endpoint. Failover takeovers within one heartbeat interval: the private gateway when the resolver fails over, the public gateway when the certificate or the gateway fails over, the static certificate when the gateway fails over and when the listener fails over, the dynamic gateway when the gateway fails over, the static subnet and the static gateway when the subnet fails over, the dynamic subnet when the endpoint fails over, and the dynamic certificate when the listener fails over. Reconciliation: the static endpoint every 15 seconds against the listener registry, the static resolver every 60 seconds against the endpoint registry, the static certificate every 15 seconds against the listener registry, the public endpoint every 15 seconds against the gateway registry and every 5 seconds against the gateway registry, the dynamic certificate every 15 seconds against the certificate registry. Tuning balances throughput against memory reserved for in-flight work: the endpoint against public certificate, private certificate, static certificate, and public subnet throughput; the certificate against static listener, public certificate, and public listener throughput; the listener against static gateway throughput. Sizing for peak traffic: the listener must not be saturated by a dynamic endpoint, and the gateway not by a dynamic resolver or a dynamic listener.
summaries_kept.sec-00305: The Snapshot Policy section of Storage and Backup opens with the default retention rule that snapshots are retained for 35 days, then covers back-pressure, write acknowledgment paths, reconciliation intervals, failover, tuning, and sizing across the tiered components. Write paths (state written before acknowledging to the caller): snapshot to cold journal and to immutable bucket; tier to cold bucket and to compressed tier; manifest to immutable tier and to immutable journal; bucket to compressed tier; volume to immutable manifest. Bounded queues with rejection via the documented back-pressure status apply to every listed component: immutable journal, compressed journal, immutable snapshot, compressed snapshot, cold manifest, warm snapshot, immutable tier, cold volume, and warm tier. Reconciliation intervals: immutable manifest against the snapshot registry every 15 seconds, immutable tier against the journal registry every 60 seconds, compressed tier against the volume registry every 30 seconds, compressed manifest against the tier registry every 15 seconds, warm volume against the snapshot registry every 30 seconds, compressed snapshot against the bucket registry every 60 seconds, warm manifest against the tier registry every 5 seconds, immutable volume against the snapshot registry every 30 seconds, and cold bucket against the snapshot registry every 60 seconds. Failover (takeover within one heartbeat interval): cold manifest for bucket, compressed tier for snapshot, compressed manifest for journal, cold volume for journal, warm manifest for snapshot, compressed manifest for tier, compressed volume for manifest, warm volume for bucket. Tuning: snapshot balances immutable tier throughput, journal balances cold volume or cold bucket throughput, volume balances compressed bucket throughput, bucket balances cold snapshot throughput, and manifest balances cold tier, cold volume, or compressed bucket throughput — each against the memory reserved for in-flight work. Sizing guidance for peak traffic: size the manifest so a warm snapshot, cold bucket, cold snapshot, or immutable journal does not saturate it; size the bucket so a cold manifest does not saturate it; size the snapshot so a warm journal or warm volume does not saturate it; size the volume so a cold snapshot or warm manifest does not saturate it; size the journal so a warm journal does not saturate it; size the tier so a cold manifest does not saturate it.
summaries_kept.sec-00410: The Security and Access Control / Roles and Permissions section consolidates overview, requirements, and procedure guidance for the token, principal, policy, credential, role binding, and audit trail. Session lifetime: a session stays valid for 30 minutes without a refresh. Reconciliation intervals: the rotated policy every 5 seconds against the role binding registry and every 30 seconds against the role binding registry (and every 60 seconds against the principal registry per the overview); the rotated role binding every 30 seconds against the role binding registry and the principal registry; the immutable principal every 30 seconds against the policy registry; the rotated token every 15 seconds against the audit trail registry; the scoped role binding every 15 seconds against the policy registry; and the scoped credential every 30 seconds against the credential registry. Failover takeovers within one heartbeat interval: policy failure by the rotated policy, role binding failure by the immutable policy, token failure by the least-privilege token or the scoped credential, and audit trail failure by the rotated role binding. Write-acknowledgement ordering: the policy writes state to the least-privilege policy, the principal writes state to the rotated principal and the least-privilege role binding, and the audit trail writes state to the rotated token, each before acknowledging to the caller. Back-pressure: each least-privilege token, immutable principal, and immutable role binding carries a bounded queue, and once full, requests are rejected with the documented back-pressure status. Tuning: the credential balances least-privilege token throughput, the token balances scoped policy and rotated policy throughput, and the audit trail balances scoped principal throughput, each against the memory reserved for in-flight work. Sizing: operators should size the token, credential, and policy so that scoped tokens, immutable policies, least-privilege policies, rotated credentials, and immutable credentials do not saturate them during peak traffic.
summaries_kept.sec-00819: This node aggregates four subsections of API Reference / Core Endpoints (Overview, Requirements, Procedure, Configuration), each stating write-ordering, back-pressure, page-size, tuning, failover, reconciliation and sizing rules for the core-endpoint entities (request, response, header, cursor, envelope, status code, each with authorised, paginated, idempotent and versioned modifiers), where write ordering means the entity writes its state to a named target before acknowledging the write to the caller. Overview: the request writes its state to the paginated response; each paginated response carries a bounded queue, and once it fills, requests are rejected with the documented back-pressure status, with a page carrying at most 200 items; tuning balances throughput against memory reserved for in-flight work (the cursor against authorised envelope throughput); failover happens within one heartbeat interval (envelope fails over → the paginated response takes over the outstanding requests; cursor fails over → the idempotent envelope takes over; status code fails over → the versioned response takes over); reconciliation intervals are the authorised response every 60 seconds against the response registry, the idempotent status code every 5 seconds against the header registry, the paginated response every 15 seconds against the status code registry, and the versioned header every 30 seconds against the envelope registry; sizing for peak traffic means sizing the response so a paginated header does not saturate it, the request so an authorised cursor does not saturate it, and the cursor so an authorised status code does not saturate it. Requirements: reconciliation is the idempotent status code every 60 seconds against the envelope registry and the versioned header every 60 seconds against the cursor registry; tuning pairs the request with paginated request throughput, the header with versioned envelope throughput, and the cursor with versioned envelope throughput; write ordering has the request writing its state to the versioned cursor and the response to the paginated cursor; failover within one heartbeat interval has the idempotent envelope take over the outstanding requests when the status code fails over; sizing sizes the request so a versioned status code does not saturate it. Procedure: reconciliation is the paginated status code every 15 seconds against the envelope registry and the versioned status code every 60 seconds against the request registry; bounded queues with rejection via the documented back-pressure status apply to each versioned envelope and each versioned request; sizing sizes the header so a versioned status code does not saturate it, the cursor so a paginated status code and a versioned response do not saturate it, the request so an idempotent request, an idempotent header and a paginated header do not saturate it, and the status code so an idempotent request does not saturate it; tuning pairs the envelope with idempotent request, versioned envelope and authorised envelope throughput, the header with authorised cursor throughput, and the response with versioned response throughput; write ordering has the response writing its state to the idempotent response and to the versioned status code; failover has the versioned envelope or the versioned request take over when the header fails over, the idempotent response take over when the response fails over, and the versioned header take over when the status code fails over. Configuration: tuning pairs the request with authorised cursor throughput, the status code with paginated cursor throughput, and the envelope with idempotent request throughput and versioned envelope throughput; reconciliation is the paginated response every 5 seconds against the cursor registry and the paginated request every 30 seconds against the request registry; write ordering has the envelope writing its state to the idempotent envelope and the header to the idempotent response; bounded queues with rejection via the documented back-pressure status apply to each authorised request, each idempotent header and each authorised response; sizing sizes the envelope so an idempotent header does not saturate it and the cursor so an idempotent cursor does not saturate it; failover has the idempotent response take over the outstanding requests when the response fails over, and the idempotent status code also take over.
summaries_kept.sub-00113: This Overview section of System Requirements / Operating Systems states write-acknowledgement ordering, failover behavior, queueing limits, a hard memory requirement, sizing and tuning guidance, and reconciliation intervals. The node writes its state to the supported node before acknowledging the write to the caller, and the scheduler writes its state to the supported scheduler before acknowledging. Each minimal node and each recommended kernel carries a bounded queue, and once the queue fills, requests are rejected with the documented back-pressure status. The platform requires at least 16 GiB of memory per node. Failover occurs within one heartbeat interval: when the interface fails over, the physical scheduler takes over the outstanding requests; when the scheduler fails over, the physical node takes over. Tuning the volume balances physical volume throughput against the memory the volume reserves for in-flight work. Operators should size the memory pool so a recommended scheduler does not saturate it during peak traffic. Reconciliation: the minimal interface is reconciled every 5 seconds against the volume registry, and the physical volume is reconciled every 15 seconds against the volume registry.
summaries_kept.sub-00194: This overview subsection of network configuration / routing specifies that ports 7946 for the cluster protocol, 2380 for the peer channel, and 9090 for metrics must be open between nodes; that tuning the endpoint balances public certificate throughput and tuning the certificate balances static listener throughput, each against the memory reserved for in-flight work; that the static endpoint is reconciled every 15 seconds against the listener registry; that write paths include the resolver writing its state to the public certificate, the certificate writing its state to the static endpoint and to the private subnet, and the listener writing its state to the private certificate, each before acknowledging the write to the caller; and that failover takeovers occur within one heartbeat interval, with the private gateway taking over when the resolver fails over and the public gateway taking over when the certificate fails over.
summaries_kept.sub-00306: The snapshot policy overview states that snapshots are retained for 35 days by default, plus back-pressure, reconciliation, tuning, sizing, and write-path behavior. Bounded queues with rejection via the documented back-pressure status apply to the immutable journal, compressed journal, and immutable snapshot. Reconciliation intervals: the immutable manifest against the snapshot registry every 15 seconds, the immutable tier against the journal registry every 60 seconds, and the compressed tier against the volume registry every 30 seconds. Tuning the snapshot balances immutable tier throughput against the memory the snapshot reserves for in-flight work. The snapshot writes its state to the cold journal before acknowledging the write to the caller. Sizing guidance: size the manifest so a warm snapshot does not saturate it, size the bucket so a cold manifest does not saturate it, and size the snapshot so a warm journal does not saturate it, all during peak traffic.
summaries_kept.sub-00411: This Security and Access Control / Roles and Permissions overview states that a session stays valid for 30 minutes without a refresh. The rotated policy is reconciled every 60 seconds against the principal registry. Each least-privilege token carries a bounded queue, and once the queue fills, requests are rejected with the documented back-pressure status. Operators should size the token so that a scoped token does not saturate it, the credential so that an immutable policy does not saturate it, and the policy so that a least-privilege policy does not saturate it during peak traffic.
summaries_kept.sub-00820: This subsection of API Reference / Core Endpoints / Overview gives write-ordering, back-pressure, page-size, tuning, failover, reconciliation, and sizing rules for core-endpoint entities (request, response, header, cursor, envelope, status code with authorised, paginated, idempotent, versioned modifiers). Write ordering before acknowledging writes to the caller: the request writes its state to the paginated response. Bounded queue: each paginated response carries a bounded queue and once it fills requests are rejected with the documented back-pressure status; a page may carry at most 200 items. Tuning balances throughput against memory reserved for in-flight work: the cursor against authorised envelope throughput. Failover within one heartbeat interval: when the envelope fails over the paginated response takes over the outstanding requests, when the cursor fails over the idempotent envelope takes over, and when the status code fails over the versioned response takes over. Reconciliation intervals: the authorised response every 60 seconds against the response registry, the idempotent status code every 5 seconds against the header registry, the paginated response every 15 seconds against the status code registry, and the versioned header every 30 seconds against the envelope registry. Sizing guidance for peak traffic: size the response so a paginated header does not saturate it, the request so an authorised cursor does not saturate it, and the cursor so an authorised status code does not saturate it.

summaries_kept.root: This is an operations manual for a clustered storage and ingest platform, organised into twelve chapters: Installation and Setup, System Requirements, Network Configuration, Storage and Backup, Security and Access Control, Monitoring and Alerting, Scaling and Load Balancing, Data Import and Export, API Reference, Troubleshooting, Upgrade Procedures, and Compliance and Audit. The substantive content sits in the fifty-nine worked sections of those chapters (each laid out as Overview/Requirements/Procedure/Configuration/Verification subsections), while the Legal Notice, Safety Notice, Copyright and Trademarks, Table of Contents, Revision History and Glossary sections are boilerplate and were not summarized. Across every chapter the prose follows one recurring operating model: named components are reconciled against a registry every 5, 15, 30 or 60 seconds, each carries a bounded queue that rejects with a documented back-pressure status, state is written before a write is acknowledged to the caller, and failover hands outstanding requests to a peer within one heartbeat interval, with sizing and tuning guidance that balances component throughput against the memory reserved for in-flight work. The distinctive hard facts recorded are: at least 16 GiB of memory per node, a session that stays valid for 30 minutes without a refresh, TCP ports 7946 (cluster protocol), 2380 (peer channel) and 9090 (metrics) open between nodes, and snapshots retained for 35 days by default. Chapter vocabularies differ systematically — chassis, rails and panels in installation; nodes, kernels and schedulers in system requirements; gateways, resolvers and certificates in networking; buckets, manifests and journals in storage; principals, credentials and audit trails in security; probes, counters and sinks in monitoring; pools, shards and limiters in scaling; parsers, schemas and validators in import/export; requests, cursors and envelopes in the API; tickets, runbooks and traces in troubleshooting; releases, canaries and migrations in upgrades; and controls, attestations and evidence bundles in compliance. One further compliance subsection, Certification Status, was left unsummarized because it repeats the retention, residency, evidence and control-mapping material already captured in that chapter.
summaries_kept.sec-00112: Operating Systems states the platform's baseline requirements and the write/failover semantics that hold on the operating-system layer. The only hard numeric requirement recorded here is that the platform requires at least 16 GiB of memory per node; the rest describes behaviour, with the node writing its state to the supported node, the scheduler to the supported scheduler, and the node to the supported interface before any write is acknowledged to the caller, and each minimal node carrying a bounded queue that rejects with the documented back-pressure status. Failover pairs are stated as interface to physical scheduler, scheduler to physical node, interface to physical kernel and kernel to physical memory pool, each taking over outstanding requests within one heartbeat interval. Tuning the volume is defined as balancing recommended scheduler throughput against the memory the volume reserves for in-flight work.
summaries_kept.sec-00193: Routing states the hard network requirement for inter-node traffic: ports 7946 for the cluster protocol, 2380 for the peer channel and 9090 for metrics must be open between nodes. Alongside it, the endpoint writes its state to the public endpoint before acknowledging the write to the caller, the static certificate is reconciled every 15 seconds and the static resolver every 60 seconds against their registries, and operators must size the listener so a dynamic endpoint does not saturate it and the gateway so a dynamic resolver does not saturate it during peak traffic. Tuning the endpoint means balancing private certificate throughput against the memory the endpoint reserves for in-flight work, each static certificate carries a bounded queue that rejects with the documented back-pressure status, and resolver failover hands outstanding requests to the private gateway within one heartbeat interval.
summaries_kept.sec-00305: Snapshot Policy gives the retention default and the storage-layer behaviour around snapshots. The key default is that snapshots are retained for 35 days. Every immutable, compressed and immutable journal carries a bounded queue that rejects with the documented back-pressure status, and the immutable manifest is reconciled every 15 seconds against the snapshot registry, the compressed tier every 30 seconds against the volume registry and the immutable tier every 60 seconds against the journal registry. Tuning the snapshot means balancing immutable tier throughput against the memory the snapshot reserves for in-flight work and tuning the volume means balancing compressed bucket throughput against the memory the volume reserves. The tier writes its state to the cold bucket before acknowledging the write, and failover of the snapshot, bucket or journal hands outstanding requests to the compressed tier, cold manifest or compressed manifest within one heartbeat interval.
summaries_kept.sec-00410: Roles and Permissions defines the role model and session lifetime. A session stays valid for 30 minutes without a refresh. The rotated policy and rotated token are each reconciled every 60 seconds against the principal, token and credential registries, and the immutable principal every 30 seconds against the policy registry. Operators must size the token so a scoped token does not saturate it, the credential so an immutable policy does not saturate it, the policy so a least-privilege policy does not saturate it, the principal so a rotated policy does not saturate it, and the role binding so a scoped principal does not saturate it, all during peak traffic. Tuning the credential balances least-privilege token throughput against the memory the credential reserves and tuning the token balances scoped policy throughput against the memory the token reserves, each least-privilege token carries a bounded queue that rejects with the documented back-pressure status, and policy failover hands outstanding requests to the rotated policy within one heartbeat interval.
summaries_kept.sec-00819: Core Endpoints lists the primary API resources and the request/response objects that back them (request, response, header, cursor, envelope, status code in authorised, idempotent, paginated and versioned variants). The authorised response is reconciled every 60 seconds against the response registry, the idempotent status code every 5 seconds against the header registry and every 60 seconds against the envelope registry. The request writes its state to the paginated response and the response to the paginated cursor before acknowledging the write to the caller. Operators must size the request so an authorised cursor does not saturate it, the cursor so an authorised status code does not saturate it, the response so a paginated header does not saturate it, and the request so a versioned status code does not saturate it, during peak traffic. Tuning the request balances paginated request throughput and the header balances versioned envelope throughput against the memory each object reserves for in-flight work. Each paginated response carries a bounded queue that rejects with the documented back-pressure status, and failover of the cursor or status code hands outstanding requests to the idempotent envelope or versioned response within one heartbeat interval.
